subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Jet Engine: Shrinking the Planet
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Jet Engine: Shrinking the Planet.

hook.text: In 1930, Frank Whittle filed a patent for the jet engine. The Air Ministry called it impractical.

buildup.text: A jet engine compresses air, mixes fuel, ignites it, and uses the exhaust to spin the compressor. Simple loop.

discovery.text: Whittle's engine ran in 1937. Meanwhile, Hans von Ohain built a similar one in Germany, independently.

twist.text: Germany flew the first jet aircraft in 1939. Britain didn't fly one until 1941. The patent holder was second.

climax.text: Today, 100,000 flights per day carry 4 billion passengers annually — all because of the jet engine.

punchline.text: One impractical idea carries 4 billion people a year.

quiz.question: Who was the first to fly a jet-powered aircraft?
options: Frank Whittle's team in Britain in 1937
Germany, using Hans von Ohain's engine in 1939
The United States Air Force in 1940
